key_insight: Three joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) formulations trained stably on longitudinal EHRs but consistently underperformed standard masked language modelling (MLM).
clinical_relevance: For research on patient representations from longitudinal EHRs, stable latent prediction alone did not yield performance competitive with MLM.
method: Adapted three JEPA formulations to predict EHR representations in latent space.
Compared their downstream performance with standard MLM using MIMIC-IV.
Examined how target size and heterogeneity affected prediction error.
evidence_signal: On MIMIC-IV, all three JEPA formulations avoided representational collapse; larger targets increased prediction error, but reducing target size did not recover downstream performance.
watch_item: The abstract reports evidence from MIMIC-IV only, leaving generalisability to other EHR datasets uncertain.
paper_title: Are Joint-Embedding Predictive Objectives Effective for Longitudinal EHRs?
